title: Performance, Security, Quality and Release Evidence

standard.family: AutoLeaP Embedded Systems Body of Knowledge

summary: Performance requirements must define the path, measurement points, workload and distribution. Average utilization does not establish latency or deadline behavior. Boot time, UI response, control loops and connectivity each need budgets and representative operating cases. Long-duration reliability also requires soak, resource-growth and recovery evidence.
learningObjectives: Build measurable system performance and reliability budgets.
Connect secure boot, isolation, vulnerability and supply-chain controls.
Lead an evidence-based release and residual-risk decision.
explanation: Performance requirements must define the path, measurement points, workload and distribution. Average utilization does not establish latency or deadline behavior. Boot time, UI response, control loops and connectivity each need budgets and representative operating cases. Long-duration reliability also requires soak, resource-growth and recovery evidence.

Security controls form a chain. Secure boot authenticates software but does not prove it is vulnerability-free. Runtime isolation constrains damage, key management supports identity and revocation, and a software bill of materials connects releases to dependency risk. Reproducible builds, protected signing and immutable metadata connect approved evidence to the field artifact.

Release readiness combines functionality, integration, timing, security, reliability, update and operational evidence. Deviations and unknowns must be explicit. Schedule pressure may motivate scope reduction, staged release or feature disablement, but it cannot substitute for an acceptability argument. Decision ownership and rollback readiness are part of the release package.
whyItMatters: Cross-layer quality problems often remain hidden when each team reports only local green metrics.
A disciplined release model protects customers and makes faster future delivery possible.
activities: Run static, dynamic, integration and fault tests
Review residual risk and containment options
Authorize signing, rollout and operational monitoring
automotiveExample: A shared platform release shows a severe memory-growth defect on one variant. The review separates affected products, validates containment, and decides to exclude that variant rather than approve a global release. Signing metadata records the eligible composition, and the OTA campaign monitors resource health during staged rollout.
commonMistakes: Equating signed software with secure software
Using average performance as a release gate
Allowing green activity metrics to hide field escapes
Accepting a deviation without owner, expiry and operational control
